Great project! Did you have any issues with the Danish oil over pine? I have a project nearly completed in pine and i wanted to try something different than the usual poly.

I find it works pretty well, you don't get much of a color change on the faces, but it'll darken the end grain more. The wood I used was pretty dry, so the end grain will really soak it up.

Not sure what sort of Danish Oil you're looking to use. The one I use is Organoil Danish Oil (you can see it in the second photo above) is really nice, it smells like oranges (citrus oil) and is food/kid safe. Some of the stuff you can buy at the hardware store reeks of solvents though.

If you're using Danish Oil, you could try rubbing it in with 400 grit wet/dry sand paper. That'll give a really nice satin finish to it.
Thanks for the recommendation, most of the big box stores carry brands that are mostly solvents. I'm trying use natural products whenever possible.
The cab is particularly aesthetically pleasing the way the wood grains line up to form a V pattern.

That was a little accidental, but quite easy to do. Effectively it's a book matched pattern.

All you need to do is to face one side (so it's flat for glue up), then cut the board in half and flip the pieces to glue them together. It's something easy to forget about, but I try to consider how the grain will look in the end result whenever I'm making stuff.
